> 知天之所為，知人之所為者，至矣。

Know what heaven does, and know what man does — that is the utmost.

大宗師 is the hinge of the inner seven. The five chapters before it loosen: dependence, judgment, vital spend, the world of men, the measure of the body. This one names what is left when all of that is loosened: 道, the teacher no person can demonstrate.

## 宗 is where everything returns

宗: the ancestral, the root, the place things go back to. 師 here is not a teacher handing down knowledge — it is what is taken as a lifelong pattern.

The book adds a line worth keeping: this 師 is not a person, so no one walks in front of you showing the way. What you have is everything walking in front of you.

## 真人 is a person with no additions

真: the unartificial, not made by man. 真人: someone not built by human manufacture, aligned with 造化 as it is.

The base sense must be fixed first, because it protects the whole chapter: 真人 is the person with nothing added, not the person with extraordinary powers. Tilt that one character and the chapter slides into hagiography — men who fly, who do not eat, who cannot be burned.

The text's own descriptions are almost aggressively ordinary: sleeping without dreams, breathing from the heels, not loving life so much as not fearing death.

## 以其所知養其所不知

The opening's real content: use what your knowing knows to nourish what it does not know, and finish your years without dying halfway.

That is not a command to know more. It is an instruction about the direction of the spend: your knowledge is a resource for the part of you that has no knowledge, not a machine for expanding itself.

## 朝徹 and 見獨

朝徹: dawn breaking, the fog clearing. After the outer layers are forgotten, the inside is suddenly clear.

見獨: 獨 is the solitary — beyond all relative pairs, with no counterpart, no reference. What is seen has no opposite, and that is why it is called 獨.

Both are descriptions of a state, not of an achievement. There is nothing to earn here; there is something to stop.

## 攖寧: the calm that grows after disturbance

攖: to disturb, to interfere. 寧: settled.

The compound means: settled inside the disturbance of ten thousand things — calm produced within commotion, not by leaving it.

The book says to bite down on the word 成 in 攖而後成. 寧 is not the state you had before the disturbance. It is what grew after it. A stillness that has never been struck is not 寧; it is merely untouched.

## 坐忘

墮肢體，黜聰明，離形去知，同於大通 — drop the body's claim, dismiss the senses' discriminations, leave form and knowledge behind, and be one with the great passage.

Note the order: form first, then knowledge. The body's claim is the earlier one.

## 畸人

畸: uneven, out of step with the world. 畸於人而侔於天 — out of step with people, level with heaven.

The word is not a consolation for the misfit. It is a description of a position: the one who does not fit the standard is the one who is not being measured by it.

## The test

What are you adding? Not acquiring — adding. One practice, one identity, one improvement project that you carry as though the self were a building under construction. 真人 is not more built. 真人 is unbuilt. Ask what would remain of you if the additions stopped today.
